title: The Morning Digest: October 18, 2026
dek: Markets are closed for the weekend, so Friday's settles remain the tape: Brent Dec26 at $109.86 and WTI Nov26 at $101.41. The refreshed validated crack history revises Friday's diesel crack close to $99.35, below $100, ending the streak above $100 at nine days; the figure printed in Saturday's edition ($104.35) came from that morning's data pull and is superseded. Friday's ICE file, which reached this run after Saturday's edition, puts WCS Dec26 at -$27.40 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 16), the widest print of the episode on thin volume, with the January to June tenors widening $1.05 to $1.20 on traded volume. SYN Nov26 settled at +$7.57 in the first session after the Syncrude coker window wrapped. Saturday was active on the war wires: Saudi-led coalition intercepts over the kingdom on Saturday and early Sunday, fires at the St. Petersburg Oil Terminal after an overnight drone attack, an escalated and still unverified Iranian mine claim, and an Iranian seven-day plan conveyed via Qatar. Riyadh airport remained without flights after its closure notice expired. On the SPR, DOE published no award for the September round but on Oct 16 re-offered up to 17 Mbbl, the remainder of the 40 Mbbl batch, implying about 23 Mbbl was taken. (Corrected after first publication: the original version described Saturday as quiet and the SPR round as simply pending; both were superseded by Oct 16-17 reporting.)
